page_summary: This page discusses the need for effective cybersecurity governance in ports, emphasizing accountability, compliance, and resource allocation. It highlights the lack of a binding global framework for port cybersecurity and notes that many countries have inadequate legislation. Recommendations include establishing a national cybersecurity framework and mandatory incident reporting. The practice section stresses the importance of proactive risk management and integrating cybersecurity into business continuity planning, particularly in high-income countries, while noting the challenges faced by low- and middle-income countries.
